Hi @icrayix !

Thank you for using Hono.

> apart from the kind of insufficient docs LOL

Ha, Ha. We have to write more good documents.

> The thing I wanted to ask is the state of the already created 3rd-party middleware. I've already found the corresponding repo but that seems pretty empty.

There are some middleware managed in every independent repository:

* https://github.com/honojs/graphql-server
* https://github.com/honojs/sentry
* https://github.com/honojs/firebase-auth

We want to move these repositories to monorepo, this repository:

https://github.com/honojs/middleware

We can't do that yet. Nevertheless, the above monorepo has a minimal setup, so adding new middleware may be easy if we want to do so.

> So yeah just wanted to know if any of the above-mentioned middleware has already been created?

No, not yet. Some of them are still in the idea stage, but others like [tRPC](https://github.com/honojs/hono/issues/582) could be implemented already

> Just wondering, why is that?

Mainly the main maintainer (me) should do that, but I don't have time. I'm not a full-time open-source developer.

> So is that repo actually open for contributions?

Yes, it's open. You can create PR for the repository.
WebSocket support.

It might sound strange, but I would prefer **not** to see more middleware. Since it's for workers which interprets code on the fly, it's IMHO better to be minimalistic rather than risking the bloat of having too many features. I find the current list of middleware really hits the sweet spot, and I would really think twice about adding something. I think it is very wise to keep the more exotic ones (especially connections to 3rd party services) in separate repositories like you did.

If there was one thing I'd say I miss, it's generating an OpenAPI spec out of the box, or through a middleware. Although I don't use them currently, I can see websocket support as a nice addition too.

Regarding the validation, that's one thing I'm not really a fan of. I prefer to validate in the endpoint itself using a more powerful lib like https://github.com/grantila/suretype where you get both the validation, the typing, can produce schemas, etc.

Given that Hono is a lightweight, full-featured, isomorphic etc... framework, I think a natural evolution would be if it could replace [Google Workbox](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/workbox/) for doing PWA-type stuff. 

In particular, allowing for entire apps (both SPAs and MPAs) to be completely templated and rendered in the browser Service worker would result in considerably faster load times as well as allow for full-featured offline usage. I assume it could be abstracted in such a way that the Cache/KV equivalents in CF Workers, Deno etc... could be plugged-in seamlessly.

It looks like there was a small previous effort to do this in Hono with the [Service Worker Magic](https://github.com/yusukebe/service-worker-magic) repo, but it doesn't seem to have found much success or traction. 

Yet, there's been various very successful efforts at this in the past, by the creator of Workbox (who has unfortunately moved on to another phase in his career).

https://jeffy.info/2017/01/24/offline-first-for-your-templated-site-part-2.html 
https://developer.chrome.com/blog/beyond-spa
https://jeffy.info/2021/07/17/sw-rendering.html (this is literally a discussion with a Cloudflare employee about how to do isomorphic templating in CF workers and Browser Service Worker)

And here's a fantastic recent effort which uses streams, iterators, template literals etc..., but its quite hand-rolled and build-free (which limits its compatibility with Hono and other TS libraries)
https://dev.to/thepassle/service-worker-side-rendering-swsr-cb1
https://thepassle.netlify.app/blog/service-worker-templating-language-(swtl)
 - https://www.npmjs.com/package/swtl (here's the `swtl` npm package for that blog)

[https://thepassle.netlify.app/blog/i-o](https://thepassle.netlify.app/blog/i-overengineered-my-blog)


Likewise, there's these two great Cloudflare blog posts from a couple years ago about doing fragment templating/composition/streaming in CF Workers. 
https://blog.cloudflare.com/better-micro-frontends/
https://blog.cloudflare.com/fragment-piercing/


All the primitives are essentially already there in Hono/web standards to replicate Workbox in Hono, and some already exist like [Routing](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/workbox/modules/workbox-routing) and [Streams](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/workbox/modules/workbox-streams).

It just needs things like [Caching Strategies](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/workbox/modules/workbox-strategies) to integrate it with the Browser Cache and IndexedDB/KV store, [background sync](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/workbox/modules/workbox-background-sync), etc... In fact, SWTL has [caching strategies](https://github.com/thepassle/swtl/blob/main/packages/core/strategies.js) already 

Here's [all of the modules](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/workbox/modules)

It seems quite clear to me that this is the future of web apps, as is Hono. So, I hope that something can be implemented here! I'd be happy to discuss and assist with this in a separate issue and PR if there's interest.

Hey everyone! 🚀 Thrilled to announce the release of `hono-openapi` – a new middleware that brings OpenAPI schema support in a middleware-like manner to Hono apps! 🎉 It's designed to help you generate OpenAPI specs effortlessly while offering flexibility with multiple validators like Zod, Typebox, and Valibot. Would love to hear your thoughts and feedback on this one too! Check it out here: https://github.com/rhinobase/hono-openapi
